references.text: The same ritual is described for the priest's sin offering - the blood is applied to the horns of the incense altar and the remainder is poured out at the base of the burnt offering altar
The blood from the sin offering for a leader is applied to the horns of the burnt offering altar, a parallel ritual
The same procedure with the blood for a sin offering from an ordinary person - on the altar's horns and the remainder at its base
Repetition of the blood ritual in the sin offering - the blood on the horns and the remainder at the base of the altar
Moses performs the same ritual at the consecration of Aaron - blood on the altar's horns and the remainder at its base
Aaron performs the blood ritual during his first service - the blood on the horns and the remainder at the base of the altar
On the Day of Atonement, blood is applied to the altar's horns to cleanse it
Instructions for the blood ritual at the altar - the blood on the horns and the remainder at its base
Annual atonement on the horns of the incense altar with the sin offering's blood
Ezekiel's temple vision includes blood on the altar's horns and at its base for cleansing
The book of Hebrews explains that almost everything is cleansed with blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness
